findings: Five address inputs have no associated label in the rendered DOM.
Connect visible labels to unique input IDs; add autocomplete, required semantics and linked error messages. Test with keyboard and a screen reader.
Quantity and remove controls appear as unnamed buttons in the accessibility snapshot.
Give each an action and product-specific accessible name. Label the quantity input.
The fit table says “Not supplied” for child height; sizes 4 and 6 are mapped to broad age bands.
Obtain supplier measurements and size conventions. Show height in cm, fit notes and how to measure. Never fabricate measurements or treat age as a guaranteed fit.
The three local fixtures expose QA titles and descriptions, single generated images and sparse size coverage.

Keep fixtures identifiable in development. Before launch, use verified product names, real stock, accurate photos, materials, care and fit information. Seed a larger representative demo catalogue separately to stress-test layouts.
Cart promises delivery within 24 hours before an address is supplied; checkout initially labels the subtotal as Total.
Use destination-dependent delivery estimates. Label pre-shipping amounts clearly and show when shipping will be calculated. Verify free-delivery messaging against the actual shipping rules.
The filter drawer has no visible Close or Show results control in the inspected state; Escape does dismiss it.
Add a labelled close button and a sticky bottom “Show N items” action. Make selection/application behaviour explicit. Keep reset secondary.
The floating WhatsApp control competes with lower-right product and page content.
Use a smaller, static help trigger; avoid product actions and safe-area edges. Hide or reposition it while menus, filters and checkout controls are active.
A prominent Sale nav item leads to zero products and a generic filter error message.
Hide Sale when no qualifying stock exists, or show a deliberate “No offers right now” state with a useful new-arrivals link.
The standalone product title is an h2; breadcrumb, back control and title repeat information.
Use one h1 on standalone product pages. Keep a compact breadcrumb and a clear title/price/options/purchase sequence. Preserve context when returning to the catalogue.
Available options, unavailable options, card edges and the disabled purchase action are all very pale.
Strengthen enabled-control boundaries; distinguish selected, unavailable and disabled states using border, text and shape as well as colour. Measure final contrast.
Azani shows one product photo; the benchmark exposes a second close-up below its first image.
Add front, back, texture and on-body views when available. Support zoom and accessible thumbnails. Keep the selected colour tied to the displayed photograph.
Fixture description does not answer shopper questions; “No reviews yet” consumes prime purchase-panel space.
Lead with material, comfort, fit, care and garment details. Move empty reviews below the purchase area; show ratings only when backed by real reviews.
A large title block and wide permanent filter sidebar consume product-discovery space.
Make title/count compact. At wide desktop use three or four well-sized products per row as available, with a narrower collapsible sidebar or filter drawer. Keep two columns on phones.
Azani’s catalogue categories are small icon/text rows; the benchmark offers photo category shortcuts.

Add compact garment-photo shortcuts above the grid: Tops, Bottoms, Dresses & Jumpsuits, Sets & Outfits, Knitwear & Outerwear, Sleepwear, Underwear & Socks. Reflect available inventory rather than creating dead ends.
Title, description, count, sort and a separate Filters row push shopping down the screen.
Use a concise title/count followed by one Filter + Sort toolbar; avoid repeating the age guidance on every listing. Keep active filters visible as removable chips.
Several select controls create the feeling of a form rather than browsing clothes.
Use collapsible groups, size buttons, labelled colour swatches and meaningful counts. Prioritise size/availability. Retain accessible native controls where they are clearer.
Desktop search starts behind an icon; mobile search is inside the menu.

Make search immediately reachable on mobile and consider a visible desktop field as inventory grows. Add clear query, result and no-result states; suggestions are a proposal, not tested functionality.
NEW, stock text, tiny sizes, title, price and an underlined size link all compete in a small card.
Use photo → name → price → available colours/sizes → action. Reserve urgency for real low stock. Keep the whole card navigable without making nested controls ambiguous.
Desktop purchase panel is clear in structure but opening size guidance pushes the action down.
Design a phone purchase area with a persistent size/action control that never hides price or errors. Use a sheet for a longer fit guide. Verify with the soft keyboard open.
The Qty column heading is separated from the actual quantity control under the product name; the right column dominates a one-item cart.
Align column labels with their controls or use an intentional item-card layout. Keep item details, editing, totals and checkout in a tighter scan path.
The full shopping navigation and large footer surround an already multi-step form.
Use a restrained checkout shell: brand, back-to-cart, help and progress. Keep guest checkout obvious and put the order summary within easy reach on mobile.
Warm-white fields have extremely faint outlines on white panels.
Use clearly visible field borders, consistent heights and strong focus rings. Reserve placeholder text for examples rather than labels.
Product name is truncated early in the narrow summary, while price appears repeatedly.
Allow a useful two-line name and explicit Size/Colour labels; show unit price, quantity and line total without redundant price rows.
Azani is friendly, but repeated pastel containers make utility screens feel more decorative than needed.
Aim for a warm kids clothing boutique: calm shopping surfaces, joyful photography and small brand accents. Ensure older children aged 9–12 are represented, not just toddler aesthetics.
Pink, blue, yellow, green and slate currently serve both decoration and utility.
Keep warm ivory/white as the base, slate for text, raspberry for the primary action. Use pale blue/blush/butter for editorial sections; reserve green for success and red for errors.
Pill inputs, pill links, rounded cards, large panels and the hero arch share attention without a clear hierarchy.
Proposed tokens: 8px inputs and image corners; 12px cards/dialogs; 20px editorial tiles; full pills only for chips and primary brand CTAs. Keep the arch as one homepage motif.
Navigation uses a dress/shirt, category filters use sparkles/cloud, and utilities use another size/emphasis.

Use one stroke family, consistent optical size and 1.5–2px strokes. Use clothing-shaped category icons or photography; keep sparkles for New In. Keep the requested coloured navigation icons, with quieter monochrome utility icons.
A dress stands for all girls’ clothing and a shirt for all boys’ clothing.

Retain readable labels; treat icons as decorative rather than exclusive category definitions. Consider neutral child portraits only if real brand assets support them. Do not make colour or an icon carry meaning alone.
Friendly headings work; secondary labels, stock text and utility copy become small and faint.

Keep Nunito for editorial headings and Geist for shopping/form text. Proposed scale: 14–16px body, 12px minimum supporting metadata, 28–36px section headings, 40–56px hero depending on viewport. Test real long names.
Large empty areas coexist with tightly packed metadata and tiny links.
Use a 4/8px spacing system: 16px mobile page gutters, 24–32px desktop gutters, 12–16px grid gaps, 32–56px section spacing. Give related controls proximity; avoid adding a box to create grouping.
Whole-card borders and rounded bottoms make the grid look like a dashboard of widgets.
Explore borderless product cards with a softly rounded image only, aligned text and stable card heights. Preserve the 3:4 garment image ratio.
A single flat-lay shirt is enlarged into the main campaign image and dominates the first mobile viewport.
Use an original lifestyle image representing the target age range, supported by clear garment photos. Shorten the mobile hero so an age/category entry appears sooner. Keep one primary CTA.
Category images are tinted by their pastel tile treatment.
Keep garment colours accurate against a consistent neutral background; apply colour around the image rather than through it.
The same small fixture assortment supplies hero, categories and product cards.
Merchandise a coherent, varied demo or real collection. Avoid repeating the same three garments in every section; do not invent bestsellers or reviews.
The icon nav is friendly but search and account controls are visually secondary and compact.

Keep icon-plus-label navigation, an obvious current destination and generous click targets. Test desktop just above the mobile breakpoint and long labels. Consider a more visible search entry before adding more nav destinations.
Large repeated navigation lists include Checkout as a general link and placeholder-looking contact details.
Use Shop, Help and About groups; remove general Checkout navigation. Publish verified support contacts, response hours, delivery/returns and size-help links. Collapse groups on mobile.
Promo code occupies its own large panel between totals and the checkout action.
Collapse it behind “Have a promo code?” so checkout remains the dominant next step. Keep feedback inline when expanded.
The site mixes “Shop All”, “All Clothing”, “Browse”, “New In” and “New arrivals”; sizes are plain numbers.
Choose consistent task labels and sentence case. Explain the real size system, e.g. years or supplier sizes, without inferring units from a number. Simplify “1 item (1 units)”.
The promotional text rotates and the help control has an attention-catching halo.
Use restrained motion, honour reduced-motion preferences and avoid animated attention cues beside purchase controls.
The form is straightforward, but borders are faint and the full footer follows immediately.
Keep sign-in compact, improve field/focus visibility, and make the password reveal control clearly labelled. Verify Google sign-in separately before featuring it as a primary route.
Prices consistently include .00 and sit beside small metadata.
Choose one local-currency display convention; consider whole-shilling display for whole prices while preserving exact values where needed. Keep price prominent and sale maths unambiguous.
Delivery and return reassurance is repeated but not always specific to the order.
Show a short accurate returns summary and delivery estimate at the decision point; link to detail rather than repeat generic promises.
This pass captured selected flows, not every input/error/loading state.

Test search suggestions, empty wishlist/cart, keyboard focus, Back/Forward restoration, filter combinations, image failures, loading shifts, validation and payment recovery before claiming release readiness.
No production performance run, complete screen-reader audit or measured contrast inventory was conducted.
Set image budgets, responsive image sizes and layout-stability targets; measure contrast and focus; test 200% zoom, 320px widths, touch targets and reduced motion on real devices.
steps: Photo category rail, restrained image corners, consistent product photography and immediately reachable search. Do not copy its adult/baby taxonomy into an ages 2–12 store.
Grouped filter controls and a persistent Apply action. Sorting takes substantial vertical space; Azani can be more concise.
Readable navigation and garment imagery, but large title/sidebar surfaces reduce browsing space. Only two matching fixtures were present.
Clear option sequence and honest sold-out state; single image, QA content and very faint controls.
Measurement values are not supplied. This is a data problem as well as a presentation problem.
Prominent checkout action. Quantity/header mismatch, unnamed controls and an unconditional delivery estimate need attention. Existing local cart was inspected; no order was created.
Signup overlay obscures product selection. Captured intentionally as a negative benchmark example.
Clear progression but weak input boundaries and missing label associations confirmed in the DOM. Later payment/review steps were not completed.
Large photo, strong price and purchase action, size guide and material/care sections. The observed default size should not override Azani’s explicit size-choice policy.
Warm palette and distinctive heading. Repeated fixture imagery and oversized hero reduce assortment storytelling.
Measured phone viewport 388 CSS px. No horizontal overflow was observed. The hero consumes the first screen before age/category discovery.
Two-column grid works. Title/filter area and help overlay compete with merchandise. Some browser captures include unused margins; these are capture artifacts, not asserted page overflow.
No visible dedicated Close/Show results controls in the captured state. Escape dismissal was verified.
Matching icons and readable labels. Search is hidden until opening the menu; age links consume a large vertical group.
Measured at 919 CSS px; this is not a phone audit. Narrow category/navigation rows continue horizontally.
No sale fixtures exist; the generic filter-recovery message does not match the shopper’s intent.
Simple login choices, pale input borders, long footer. No login, account creation or password reset submitted.
